headline: FBI ties record $6.43B Binance heist to North Korea's TraderTraitor; Ivanti KEV deadline tomorrow; Polymarket drained via DebugBear script

bullets.text: New since the last SITREP: the FBI has linked North Korea's TraderTraitor group to the record Binance crypto heist, now put at $6.43 billion. Binance earlier tied the theft to a compromised DevOps laptop.
New since the last SITREP: hackers stole about $2.7 million from Polymarket traders through a hijacked third-party DebugBear script.

Attackers are chaining three Ivanti Connect Secure flaws (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527) to gain unauthenticated root access. The first CISA KEV due date for Ivanti Connect Secure is tomorrow, 2026-11-02; the second is 2026-11-13.
KEV due dates for the exploited GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229 and the Cisco ASA/FTD flaw CVE-2026-76418 (used to crash SSL VPN devices) fell today, 2026-11-01. Unpatched instances are now overdue.
The official Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace was trojanized with a persistent SSH backdoor; WIRED reports it reached thousands of developer devices.
A Northflank security breach has led to abuse of customers' AI API keys, and Chainalysis confirmed an intrusion that exposed customer identity data.

actions: Patch Ivanti Connect Secure before the 2026-11-02 KEV deadline and check appliances for signs of the chained root compromise.
If GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) or Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) are still unpatched, treat them as overdue and patch now.
Inventory third-party scripts on your web apps, including DebugBear, and check for unexpected changes to what they load.
If you store AI provider API keys in Northflank, rotate them and review provider usage and billing for abuse.
If developers use the Claude Code extension in Cursor, check it against the vendor advisory and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.
Update Drupal Commerce Core for the actively exploited CVE-2026-118539 and check sites for unauthorized access.
